profile.summary: BioFM is a genomic foundation model from M42 Health that reads DNA together with biological context. Its BioToken tokeniser encodes genetic variants and annotated regions (such as genes and regulatory elements) directly in the input, instead of treating DNA as bases only. The model produces embeddings for variants or sequences, which are used with simple classifiers to predict effects on expression, splicing and pathogenicity; it can also generate DNA sequence.
profile.summary_source_locator: Europe PMC abstract; model card: Model Details; README: Quick Start

summary_quotes.text: Here, we introduce BioToken, a modular and extendable tokenization framework designed to encode genomic variants and biologically relevant region annotations directly into genomic representations.

Current GFMs typically treat DNA simplistically as nucleotide-only sequences, overlooking critical biological context, such as genomic annotations, regulatory elements, and functional contexts central to genomic interpretation.
such as gene expression, alternative splicing, and variant pathogenicity prediction
BioFM can generate genomic sequences based on input DNA prompts.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: BioFM is a decoder-only (causal) transformer on the Mistral architecture, with 23 layers and hidden size 640. The paper says the authors kept Mistral's grouped-query attention, disabled its sliding-window attention so the model sees the whole input, and raised the RoPE frequency parameter to handle longer DNA. Its input is DNA annotated with BioTokens: special variant tokens replace the standard bases at single nucleotide variants and insertions, and further tokens mark transcript boundaries, exons and coding sequences. During pretraining, half of the inputs were reverse complemented. For a variant, the package builds an upstream and a downstream sequence, each ending at the variant and half the evaluation context long; the downstream one is reverse complemented. Reference and mutated embeddings are each averaged over the two directions and then concatenated, giving a vector twice the embedding size. For plain sequences the embedding is taken from the last token. Downstream predictions use linear probing on these embeddings.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: One checkpoint is released: m42-health/BioFM-265M. A result should name it and its Hugging Face revision; this page read revision 52218bbd. The biofm-eval package is version 0.1.0. The README includes a script to reproduce the paper's variant benchmark by linear probing on the m42-health/variant-benchmark dataset with chromosome-based folds. Training ran on an NVIDIA DGX cluster with H100 GPUs using PyTorch FSDP. The paper's ablations used a smaller 67M-parameter model, which is not among the released checkpoints in the saved files; the paper says the training code is adapted from Meta's llama-cookbook.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Decoder-only (causal) genomic foundation model with biologically informed tokenisation (BioToken).
facts.source_locator: Model card: Model Details; README: Creating Variant Embeddings

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Mistral causal transformer: 23 layers, hidden size 640, 32 attention heads with 8 key-value heads, vocabulary of 512 tokens.

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: DNA sequences annotated with BioTokens. For variants: a VCF file or a single variant (chromosome, position, reference and alternate base), plus a GENCODE gene annotation GFF3 and the GRCh38 reference FASTA. Plain DNA strings are also accepted for sequence embeddings and generation.
facts.source_locator: Model card: Model Details; README: Quick Start

quotes.text: - **Input format:** Annotated DNA sequences using BioToken

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Embeddings (variant embeddings of shape 2 x embedding size; sequence embeddings from the last token) and generated DNA sequences.

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: Whole-genome sequences of 50 individuals from the 1000 Genomes Project (10 from each of the five superpopulations, chosen from 3,202 samples), Phase 3 data on the HG38 assembly, autosomes and the X chromosome. Each individual's variants were applied to 6,144-nucleotide reference regions, with GENCODE release 38 annotations added as tokens. The paper gives about 166 billion tokens per epoch and two epochs of pretraining.

limitations.text: Variant work needs the GRCh38 reference genome and a GENCODE v38 annotation file, and the training data is human (1000 Genomes). The authors say the approach relies on high-quality annotations and variant data that other organisms may lack, and that annotation tokens may bias evaluation because eQTLs and sQTLs lie closer to transcript or exon boundaries than negative controls.

run_guide.summary: Install the biofm-eval package at a pinned commit and extract embeddings for two short DNA sequences with BioFM-265M.
prerequisites: conda, to create a Python 3.11 environment. The package requires Python >=3.11, torch>=2.5.1 and transformers>=4.46.1.
No GPU is required; the developers tested on a MacBook M2 Pro with 16GB memory and on Linux with an H100.
Code and weights are CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial). The weights are not gated.

steps.title: Create the environment
steps.shell:
conda create -n biofm-eval-env python=3.11
conda activate biofm-eval-env
steps.explanation: Creates and activates the Python 3.11 environment named in the README.

steps.title: Get the code at the pinned commit and install
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/m42-health/biofm-eval.git
cd biofm-eval
git checkout --detach fcb86e1cb699bf29d220eae173e5042ba3f4ad3d
pip install -e .
steps.explanation: The README's clone and install commands. The checkout line is added to get the commit this page was written from.

steps.title: Extract sequence embeddings
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
from biofm_eval import AnnotatedModel, AnnotationTokenizer, Embedder
import torch

MODEL_PATH = "m42-health/BioFM-265M"
TOKENIZER_PATH = "m42-health/BioFM-265M"

model = AnnotatedModel.from_pretrained(
    MODEL_PATH,
    torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
)
tokenizer = AnnotationTokenizer.from_pretrained(TOKENIZER_PATH)

embedder = Embedder(model, tokenizer)

input_sequences = ['AGCT', 'GACTGCA']
sequence_embedding = embedder.get_sequence_embeddings(input_sequences)
print(f'Embedding dimension: {sequence_embedding.shape}')
PY
steps.explanation: The README's sequence embedding example, wrapped in a shell heredoc with its comments removed. It downloads BioFM-265M and needs no other input files.
